    Optimal Sample Size Calculation for Co-Primary Diagnostic Accuracy Endpoints - Single-test design

    ss_opt_bin.Rd

    The function determines the minimal total sample size required to achieve a prespecified overall power in a confirmatory diagnostic accuracy study with co-primary endpoints (sensitivity and specificity).

    Both endpoints must demonstrate superiority over fixed null values. Overall power is defined under an intersection–union testing (IUT) framework, meaning that both null hypotheses must be rejected for the study to be successful. Under this framework, the global Type I error rate is controlled at level \(\alpha\) without multiplicity adjustment.

    The calculation explicitly accounts for disease prevalence, which determines the expected number of diseased and non-diseased subjects.

    ss_opt_bin(
  power,
  prev,
  se.e,
  se.min,
  sp.e,
  sp.min,
  alpha = 0.025,
  ci_method = c("wald", "logit"),
  alternative = c("one.sided", "two.sided")
)

    Arguments

    power

    Overall desired power

    prev

    Disease prevalence

    se.e

    Sensitivity under alternative hypothesis

    se.min

    Sensitivity under null hypothesis

    sp.e

    Specificity under alternative hypothesis

    sp.min

    Specificity under null hypothesis

    alpha

    Type I error level.

    ci_method

    Normal approximation method: "wald" (default) or "logit".

    alternative

    "one.sided" (default) or "two.sided".

    Value

    An object of class "dx_bin" containing:

    • design specifications(design specifications (alpha level, testing framework, CI method)

    • required total sample size,

    • subgroup sample sizes,

    • target overall power

    • allocated endpoint-specific powers.

    Details

    Let \(\pi\) denote the assumed disease prevalence. The study population is partitioned into diseased (\(N_{Se} = N\pi\)) and non-diseased (\(N_{Sp} = N(1-\pi)\)) independent subgroups.

    When prevalence is very low or very high, one subgroup may require substantially more subjects than the other. A naive calculation (e.g. taking the maximum of two independently calculated sample sizes) may therefore overpower one endpoint while the other determines the required total sample size.

    This function implements an optimal joint sample size calculation that balances both endpoints simultaneously. Endpoint-specific powers are allocated such that:

    • the overall power equals the target value,

    • both endpoints imply the same required total sample size,

    • neither sensitivity nor specificity is unnecessarily overpowered.

    Sample size formulas are based on large-sample normal approximations for binomial proportions using either:

    • the Wald approximation on the probability scale, or

    • the logit-transformed normal approximation.

    The endpoint-specific powers are determined numerically by solving a root-finding problem under the overall power constraint: $$ Power_{overall} = Power_{Se} \times Power_{Sp}. $$

    The methodology follows the joint sample size framework for single-arm confirmatory diagnostic accuracy studies described in Stark, M., & Zapf, A. (2020).

    In the single-test design there is no distinction between superiority and non-inferiority.

    References

    Stark, M., & Zapf, A. (2020). Sample size calculation and re-estimation based on the prevalence in a single-arm confirmatory diagnostic accuracy study. Statistical Methods in Medical Research, 29(10), 2958–2971. doi:10.1177/0962280220913588

    Author

    Ainesh Sewak & Maia Muresan (DCR Bern)

    Examples

    # Example 1: Sample size calculation for a single diagnostic test
# Objective: demonstrate that sensitivity and specificity exceed
# pre-specified minimum acceptable values
ss_opt_bin(
  power = 0.80,        # desired power
  prev = 0.5,          # disease prevalence
  se.e = 0.85,         # expected sensitivity
  se.min = 0.65,       # minimum acceptable sensitivity
  sp.e = 0.85,         # expected specificity
  sp.min = 0.55,       # minimum acceptable specificity
  alpha = 0.025        # one-sided significance level
)
#> 
#> DxPower - Confirmatory Diagnostic Accuracy Study 
#> --------------------------------------------------
#> Design:            single-test design 
#> Framework:        Co-primary (IUT)
#> Alpha level:       0.025 (one.sided) 
#> Prevalence:        0.5 
#> 
#> Hypotheses:
#>   Sensitivity :    sup 
#>   Specificity :    sup 
#> 
#> Required sample size per group:
#>   Total:           78 
#>   Diseased:        39 
#>   Non-diseased:    39 
#> 
#> Target overall power:   0.8 
#> 
#> Allocated powers:
#>   Sensitivity:      0.805 
#>   Specificity:      0.994 
#> 
#same
ss_opt_bin(
  power = 0.80,        # desired power
  prev = 0.5,          # disease prevalence
  se.e = 0.85,         # expected sensitivity
  se.min = 0.65,       # minimum acceptable sensitivity
  sp.e = 0.85,         # expected specificity
  sp.min = 0.55,       # minimum acceptable specificity
  alpha = 0.025,        # one-sided significance level (default)
  ci_method = "wald",   # default
  alternative = "one.sided" #default
)

#> 
# Example 2: Same design using logit-based confidence interval
ss_opt_bin(
  power = 0.80,
  prev = 0.5,
  se.e = 0.85,

)
